newsitem.title: UK: Export optimism helps Europe grains market tone.
newsitem.headline: Export optimism helps Europe grains market tone.

text.p: Export optimism put a more bullish tone in Europe's grains markets this week, although traders still say the EU is not moving grain fast enough.

France did best out of new deals, with Germany lagging despite a good competitive position. The UK market remains a creature of currency moves, but increased farmer selling has brightened the outlook in recent days.
Export prospects pushed French wheat prices up, with Rouen wheat for March gaining 10 francs over the previous week, dealers said. Barley and maize prices also rose with wheat.
But concern over firm French prices prevented the EU Commission parting with substantial wheat volumes at its weekly grain auction on Thursday.
Wheat prices on Friday ignored the results of the EU grain auction, with Rouen wheat steady at 865 francs per tonne.
Dealers said bids for more than one million tonnes in wheat export licences submitted on Thursday showed there was business to cover and this was supporting prices.
French wheat was helped by sales to Iran and news Algeria was in the market for 125,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat.
On Thursday Algeria bought 75,000 tonnes of French wheat under a Coface-guaranteed export credit at around $165 per tonne, cost and freight.
Support also came from large sales of EU flour, dealers said.
EU member country officials on Friday said the EU had cleared the export of more than 600,000 tonnes of EU flour over the past two weeks.

But concern over higher French prices drove the EU Commission to grant modest wheat exports at its grain auction on Thursday, member country officials said. The EU concern was to insure domestic users with affordable supplies.
"The Commission did not want to drive prices higher," one official said.
The EU granted the export of 238,000 tonnes of soft wheat at a rebate of 16.40 Ecus per tonne, nearly two Ecus below last week.
Disappointed exporters said that if the EU had reduced the export refund to just 17 Ecus it could have released 500,000 tonnes of wheat, more in line with a licence short of over one million tonnes.
They said the current export pace was insufficient to absorb the EU grain surplus before new supplies from the United States, Canada and Australia hit the market.
Exporters also said the 16.40 Ecus per tonne refund values French wheat at $146 and is insufficient to help cover sales to Iran or Egypt clinched at around $140 per tonne, fob.

On Thursday the EU awarded the import of 32,000 tonnes of maize to Spain and 90,000 tonnes of maize to Portugal at reduced tariffs but dealers said this had no impact on maize prices due to the hefty volumes awarded the previous week.

Germany's market has reacted only slowly to firmness in the UK and France. "It's now, along with Denmark, the cheapest market in Europe," one German trader said. He noted that small amounts of wheat and barley were even going into intervention.
The German market is helped by a lack of competition from other origins. "Consumers are doingh their buying on the domestic market, not importing," the trader said.
The German intervention agency BLE said on Monday that nearly 40,000 tonnes of rye were offered to its stores last week.
The British market has been highly volatile, with prices pushed this way and that by the volatility of sterling. "Up and down like a yo-yo," was one trader's description.

There was a flurry of farmer selling in midweek, in response to a jump in futures on Tuesday. Futures brokers put that jump down to optimism on the UK's cereals balance sheet, as well as a drop that day in sterling's value against continental currencies.
Spanish traders said the lorry drivers' strike brought business to a standstill. But the strike, which ended on Thursday, did not have a big effect on ex-farm prices except in isolated areas.
Maize prices slipped marginally in the northern Cataluna region where roads were badly hit by the strike.
Feed, milling and durum wheat remained largely unchanged. The durum wheat market has almost entirely dried up with clients opting for cheaper alternatives from abroad.
Barley prices were also largely stagnant

Italian cereal markets were once again calm with no big changes. Soft wheat prices fell slightly over the past week. "There was little fresh demand and the arrival of soft wheat from abroad, especially from France, depressed prices slightly", the Italian Institute for Agriculture studies (ISMEA) said.
